Key capabilities include: controlling a browser to visit and extract information from web pages; searching and downloading academic papers from arXiv; looking up content on Wikipedia; downloading YouTube videos (with automatic audio extraction); and general-purpose file downloading from URLs. function.name: PostgresManager
function.description: A database management agent responsible for inspecting, querying, and analyzing a PostgreSQL database. It can enumerate schemas and database objects, retrieve detailed metadata about tables and other objects, and execute SQL queries with read-only restrictions when applicable. function.name: DocumentAnalyzer
function.description: A comprehensive document-processing agent capable of extracting, analyzing, and structuring content from a wide range of local office files and text formats. Supports CSV/TSV, Word (DOC/DOCX), PowerPoint (PPT/PPTX), Excel (XLS/XLSX), PDF, and diverse text/code files. Designed to deliver clean, organized results for downstream reasoning and further processing. It can extract embedded media as raw files or generate screenshots for visual spreadsheet elements, which are then passed to specialized agents for further analysis.

function.name: MediaAnalyzer
function.description: A multimedia analysis agent capable of handling local images, audio, and video. It provides OCR extraction, AI-based visual understanding, metadata inspection, audio transcription and trimming, video analysis and summarization, and key-frame extraction. Supports common formats across images (JPG/PNG/GIF/TIFF/WEBP …), audio (MP3/WAV/FLAC/AAC/OGG …), and video (MP4/AVI/MOV/MKV/WEBM …). GIF and video content are processed as multi-frame sequences—similar to video key-frame extraction—while static image formats are analyzed as single frames. Designed to perform assigned multimedia tasks efficiently and return clear, structured results.

function.name: PythonExecutor

Its execution is strictly limited to the Python code and data explicitly provided to it. Useful for performing math calculations or demonstrating small code examples.

function.name: Reasoner

Summarize the main content of a video using AI analysis.

        This tool provides AI-powered video summarization with:
        - Key point extraction
        - Main topic identification
        - Important visual element recognition
        - LLM-optimized result formatting

        Args:
            video_url: The input video filepath or URL to summarize
            sample_rate: Sample n frames per second
            start_time: Start time of the video segment in seconds
            end_time: End time of the video segment in seconds
            output_format: Format for the response output

        Returns:
            ActionResponse with video summary results and metadata

video_url.description: The input video filepath or URL to summarize.
video_url.title: Video Url

start_time.description: Start time of the video segment in seconds (default: 0).
start_time.title: Start Time

end_time.description: End time of the video segment in seconds (default: None).
end_time.title: End Time

function.name: mcp_extract_keyframes
function.description:
Extract key frames around a target time with scene detection.

        This tool provides keyframe extraction with:
        - Scene detection for significant frame changes
        - Configurable time windows
        - Automatic output directory management
        - LLM-optimized result formatting

        Args:
            video_path: The input video filepath or URL
            target_time: Specific time point (in seconds) to extract frames around
            window_size: Time window (in seconds) centered on target_time
            cleanup: Whether to delete the original video file after processing
            output_dir: Directory where extracted frames will be saved
            output_format: Format for the response output

        Returns:
            ActionResponse with keyframe extraction results and metadata

video_path.description: The input video filepath or URL.
video_path.title: Video Path

target_time.description: The specific time point for extraction (in seconds), centered within the window_size.
target_time.title: Target Time

window_size.description: The window size for extraction (in seconds, default: 5).
window_size.title: Window Size

output_dir.description: Directory where extracted frames will be saved (default: workspace/keyframes).
output_dir.title: Output Dir

def square_to_coords(square):
    """Convert algebraic notation to coordinates"""
    file_map = {'a': 0, 'b': 1, 'c': 2, 'd': 3, 'e': 4, 'f': 5, 'g': 6, 'h': 7}
    rank_map = {'1': 7, '2': 6, '3': 5, '4': 4, '5': 3, '6': 2, '7': 1, '8': 0}
    file = square[0]
    rank = square[1]
    return (rank_map[rank], file_map[file])

def coords_to_square(coords):
    """Convert coordinates to algebraic notation"""
    rank, file = coords
    file_map = {0: 'a', 1: 'b', 2: 'c', 3: 'd', 4: 'e', 5: 'f', 6: 'g', 7: 'h'}
    rank_map = {7: '1', 6: '2', 5: '3', 4: '4', 3: '5', 2: '6', 1: '7', 0: '8'}
    return f"{file_map[file]}{rank_map[rank]}"

# Define piece positions from FEN
white_pieces = {
    'K': 'a1',  # King
    'Q': 'a5',  # Queen
    'R': 'd3',  # Rook
    'B': 'e3',  # Bishop
    'N': 'f3',  # Knight
    'P': ['b2', 'c2', 'h3']  # Pawns
}

black_pieces = {
    'k': 'a8',  # King
    'q': 'g3',  # Queen
    'r': 'e8',  # Rook
    'b': 'd6',  # Bishop
    'n': 'f4',  # Knight
    'p': ['a6', 'b7', 'c7', 'g7', 'h7']  # Pawns
}

print("Checking potential winning moves for black...")
print("\nConsider Qxh3+ (queen takes pawn on h3):")
print("White king must move (only to b1)")
print("Then black could follow with Qg2# (queen to g2 checkmate)")
print("But is Qxh3+ check? Let's check...")

# Check if Qxh3+ is check
white_king_pos = square_to_coords('a1')
black_queen_pos = square_to_coords('g3')
h3_pos = square_to_coords('h3')

print(f"\nWhite king at {coords_to_square(white_king_pos)}")
print(f"Black queen at {coords_to_square(black_queen_pos)}")
print(f"h3 at {coords_to_square(h3_pos)}")

# Check if queen attacks king from h3
# Queen moves horizontally, vertically, or diagonally

print("- Same file: h3 to h1, h2, h4, h5, h6, h7, h8")
print("- Diagonals: h3 to g2, f1, g4, f5, e6, d7, c8")

# a1 is at coordinates (7, 0) - that's rank 1, file a
# h3 is at coordinates (5, 7) - that's rank 3, file h
# They're not on same rank, file, or diagonal

print("So Qxh3+ is not check, just a capture")

def square_to_coords(square):
    """Convert algebraic notation to coordinates"""
    file_map = {'a': 0, 'b': 1, 'c': 2, 'd': 3, 'e': 4, 'f': 5, 'g': 6, 'h': 7}
    rank_map = {'1': 7, '2': 6, '3': 5, '4': 4, '5': 3, '6': 2, '7': 1, '8': 0}
    file = square[0]
    rank = square[1]
    return (rank_map[rank], file_map[file])

def coords_to_square(coords):
    """Convert coordinates to algebraic notation"""
    rank, file = coords
    file_map = {0: 'a', 1: 'b', 2: 'c', 3: 'd', 4: 'e', 5: 'f', 6: 'g', 7: 'h'}
    rank_map = {7: '1', 6: '2', 5: '3', 4: '4', 3: '5', 2: '6', 1: '7', 0: '8'}

{"code": "# Let's create a simple chess position analyzer manually

def square_to_coords(square):
    """Convert algebraic notation to coordinates"""
    file_map = {'a': 0, 'b': 1, 'c': 2, 'd': 3, 'e': 4, 'f': 5, 'g': 6, 'h': 7}
    rank_map = {'1': 7, '2': 6, '3': 5, '4': 4, '5': 3, '6': 2, '7': 1, '8': 0}
    file = square[0]
    rank = square[1]
    return (rank_map[rank], file_map[file])

def coords_to_square(coords):
    """Convert coordinates to algebraic notation"""
    rank, file = coords
    file_map = {0: 'a', 1: 'b', 2: 'c', 3: 'd', 4: 'e', 5: 'f', 6: 'g', 7: 'h'}
    rank_map = {7: '1', 6: '2', 5: '3', 4: '4', 3: '5', 2: '6', 1: '7', 0: '8'}
    return f"{file_map[file]}{rank_map[rank]}"

# Define piece positions from FEN
white_pieces = {
    'K': 'a1',  # King
    'Q': 'a5',  # Queen
    'R': 'd3',  # Rook
    'B': 'e3',  # Bishop
    'N': 'f3',  # Knight
    'P': ['b2', 'c2', 'h3']  # Pawns
}

black_pieces = {
    'k': 'a8',  # King
    'q': 'g3',  # Queen
    'r': 'e8',  # Rook
    'b': 'd6',  # Bishop
    'n': 'f4',  # Knight
    'p': ['a6', 'b7', 'c7', 'g7', 'h7']  # Pawns
}

print("Checking potential winning moves for black...")
print("\nConsider Qxh3+ (queen takes pawn on h3):")
print("White king must move (only to b1)")
print("Then black could follow with Qg2# (queen to g2 checkmate)")
print("But is Qxh3+ check? Let's check...")

# Check if Qxh3+ is check
white_king_pos = square_to_coords('a1')
black_queen_pos = square_to_coords('g3')
h3_pos = square_to_coords('h3')

print(f"\nWhite king at {coords_to_square(white_king_pos)}")
print(f"Black queen at {coords_to_square(black_queen_pos)}")
print(f"h3 at {coords_to_square(h3_pos)}")

# Check if queen attacks king from h3
# Queen moves horizontally, vertically, or diagonally
print("\nFrom h3, queen would attack:")
print("- Same rank: h3 to a3, b3, c3, d3, e3, f3, g3")
print("- Same file: h3 to h1, h2, h4, h5, h6, h7, h8")
print("- Diagonals: h3 to g2, f1, g4, f5, e6, d7, c8")

# a1 is at coordinates (7, 0) - that's rank 1, file a
# h3 is at coordinates (5, 7) - that's rank 3, file h
# They're not on same rank, file, or diagonal
print("\nFrom h3, queen does NOT give check to king on a1")
print("So Qxh3+ is not check, just a capture")

print("\nLet's check other candidate moves:")

print("2. Nxg2+? Knight to g2 check (attacks king on a1? No)")
print("3. Re1+? Rook to e1 check")
print("4. Nxd3+? Knight takes rook with discovered check?")
print("5. Qf2+? Queen to f2 check (mate threat)")", "session_id": 1773993885}

    rank_map = {'1': 7, '2': 6, '3': 5, '4': 4, '5': 3, '6': 2, '7': 1, '8': 0}
    file = square[0]
    rank = square[1]
    return (rank_map[rank], file_map[file])

    """Convert coordinates to algebraic notation"""
    rank, file = coords
    file_map = {0: 'a', 1: 'b', 2: 'c', 3: 'd', 4: 'e', 5: 'f', 6: 'g', 7: 'h'}
    rank_map = {7: '1', 6: '2', 5: '3', 4: '4', 3: '5', 2: '6', 1: '7', 0: '8'}
